chunks: What Zur‘ah narrated from al-Mufaddal, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“My father عليه السلام would separate between Shaʿbān and the month of Ramaḍān by a day, while ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام would join them, and he would say: ‘Fasting two consecutive months is a repentance from Allah.’”

key_terms.تَوْبَةٌ: Repentance; a means of turning back to Allah.
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramaḍān, the obligatory month of fasting.
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: The month of Shaʿbān, the month preceding Ramaḍān.
key_terms.صَوْمُ: Fasting, the devotional act being discussed.
key_terms.مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: Consecutive, without interruption between the two months.
key_terms.يَصِلُ: He would join; here, by continuing fasting from one month into the next.
key_terms.يَفْصِلُ: He would separate; here, by leaving a day between the two months.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about joining Shaʿbān to Ramaḍān with fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith reports two practices among the Imams عليهم السلام regarding the end of Shaʿbān and the beginning of Ramaḍān: one separating them by a day, and the other joining them through continuous fasting. It also highlights the spiritual meaning of fasting two consecutive months as an expression of repentance from Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1827 - It is narrated by Zur‘ah from al-Mufaddal, from Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)), who said:

"My father (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as)) would separate between Sha‘ban and Month of Ramadan by a day, while Ali ibn al-Husayn (as) would join them and say: ‘Fasting two consecutive months is repentance from Allah (swt).’”
